from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Lifeguards must reach drowning swimmers quickly.",
            "Running on sand is slower than swimming.",
            "A straight path is not always fastest.",
            "We seek the path of least time.",
            "Angle impacts total travel time."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The 'Life Guard' Problem", lecture_lines)

        # Visual Setup
        boundary = Line(LEFT*3 + UP*0, RIGHT*3 + UP*0, color=WHITE)
        beach = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_opacity=0.3, color="#F0E68C").next_to(boundary, UP, buff=0)
        ocean = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_opacity=0.3, color="#4682B4").next_to(boundary, DOWN, buff=0)
        
        # Grid placement
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(beach, ocean, boundary), 'D3', scale_factor=0.6)

        # Lifeguard and Swimmer
        lifeguard = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(self.grid['A2'])
        swimmer = Dot(color=RED).move_to(self.grid['F5'])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(beach), FadeIn(ocean), Create(boundary), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(lifeguard), FadeIn(swimmer), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GOLD)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        path_straight = Line(lifeguard.get_center(), swimmer.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(path_straight), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        path_opt = VMobject()
        path_opt.set_points_smoothly([lifeguard.get_center(), self.grid['C4'], swimmer.get_center()])
        path_opt.set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Create(path_opt), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Representing [Asset: LifeguardPathAnimation] via changing intersection
        dot_intersection = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(self.grid['C4'])
        self.play(dot_intersection.animate.move_to(self.grid['C3']), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Apply Fermat’s Principle: minimize total time.",
            "Set the derivative to zero.",
            "Result: n1 sin theta1 = n2 sin theta2.",
            "This confirms the law of refraction.",
            "Light chooses the fastest path."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Deriving Snell’s Law via Fermat's Principle", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        math_eq = MathTex(r"\frac{dT}{dx} = \frac{\sin\theta_1}{v_1} - \frac{\sin\theta_2}{v_2} = 0", font_size=36)
        snell_law = MathTex(r"n_1 \sin\theta_1 = n_2 \sin\theta_2", font_size=40, color=YELLOW)
        box = SurroundingRectangle(snell_law, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(math_eq, "B3")
        self.play(Write(math_eq))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        # Visual cue for setting to zero
        self.play(Indicate(math_eq[0][-1]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(math_eq, snell_law))
        self.play(Create(box))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Indicate(VGroup(snell_law, box)))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(TEAL))
        self.play(Flash(snell_law, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Refraction follows the path of least time.", "The lifeguard analogy holds true for light.", "Nature optimizes to find efficiency."]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Real-world Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for lines

        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])

outline.topic: The Physics of Refraction: A Proof of Snell's Law
outline.target_audience: University Physics Students / Advanced High School Physics Students

sections.title: Introduction: The 'Life Guard' Problem
sections.content: Introduce refraction by framing it as an optimization problem: a lifeguard on a sandy beach needs to reach a swimmer in the water as fast as possible. Since running on sand is slower than swimming in water, the lifeguard must choose an angle that minimizes total travel time.
sections.example: Visual animation showing a lifeguard choosing a straight line (short distance, long time in sand) vs. an angled path (longer distance, shorter time in sand).

sections.title: Prerequisite Geometry: Defining the Interface
sections.content: Establish the coordinate system: two media with refractive indices n1 and n2, separated by a flat boundary. Define incident angle (θ1) and refracted angle (θ2) relative to the normal line.
sections.example: A split-screen graphic: Top half is air (n1), bottom half is water (n2), with a dashed vertical 'normal' line intersecting the boundary.

sections.title: Mathematical Formulation of Time
sections.content: Express the total time (T) as a function of distance and speed (v = c/n). T = (d1 / v1) + (d2 / v2). Introduce the variable 'x' as the distance along the boundary to the refraction point.
sections.example: An interactive diagram where moving the refraction point 'x' updates the equation T(x) in real-time.

sections.title: Deriving Snell’s Law via Fermat's Principle
sections.content: Apply Fermat’s Principle of Least Time: take the derivative of T(x) with respect to x and set it to zero (dT/dx = 0). Show the resulting geometric relationship between the sines of the angles.
sections.example: Step-by-step mathematical expansion: dT/dx = (sinθ1 / v1) - (sinθ2 / v2) = 0, leading directly to n1 sinθ1 = n2 sinθ2.

sections.title: Conclusion: Real-world Synthesis
sections.content: Summarize how the proof demonstrates that light 'chooses' the path of least time. Relate this back to the lifeguard analogy to solidify the conceptual intuition.
sections.example: Show a laser beam bending through a glass block side-by-side with the lifeguard's path to demonstrate the universal nature of the law.
